headline: Life cycles are the stages from birth to death to new life—patterns that repeat across generations
universal_truth: Everything has seasons; understanding cycles helps you navigate where you are and what comes next
fun_facts: Mayflies live as adults for only 24 hours—their entire purpose is reproduction
Some jellyfish can reverse their life cycle, effectively becoming immortal
Salmon are born in freshwater, live in salt water, and return to freshwater to spawn and die
discussion_questions: What life cycle stage are you in currently?
How does understanding cycles change how you approach current challenges?
What stage is coming next for you?

hook.script: Birth, growth, reproduction, death. Every living thing follows a cycle—not a line but a circle. What dies feeds what's born. Generations connect through these repeating patterns. Life isn't just living; it's cycling.

cliff.script: Life cycles seem obvious, but they contain wisdom. Each stage has its purpose and challenges. What does thinking in cycles teach us?
cliff.prompt: What's the value of cycle thinking?

options.text: Cycles reveal that each stage is temporary and purposeful—understanding where you are helps you do that stage's work and prepare for what's next
options.response: Yes. Youth is for growth. Maturity is for contribution. Each stage has its task. Fighting your stage wastes energy; embracing it lets you complete it and move on.
They describe, but they also prescribe—each stage has appropriate work...

fact1.title: Stage-Appropriate Work
fact1.script: Each life stage has appropriate work. Young animals learn and grow. Adults reproduce and provide. Elders teach. Doing the right work at the right stage is efficiency; fighting it is waste.

fact2.title: Transition Points
fact2.script: Between stages are transitions—often difficult. Adolescence between childhood and adulthood. Retirement between work and rest. Transition is inherently uncomfortable; it's moving between stable states.

fact3.title: Generational Connection
fact3.script: Cycles connect generations. What one generation produces, the next consumes and builds upon. You're part of a cycle larger than your individual life—receiving from the past, contributing to the future.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything has seasons. Understanding cycles helps you navigate where you are and what comes next. Do the work of your current stage.

outro.script: That's Day 262. Tomorrow, we'll explore how life makes more life—reproduction. Until then, identify what stage you're in and its appropriate work.

growTrack.title: Stage Assessment - Where Are You in the Cycle?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify current life stage and appropriate work
growTrack.activity: What life stage are you in—in career, relationships, personal development? What's the appropriate work of this stage? What stage is coming next? Align your efforts with your stage for maximum effectiveness.
